reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure and canonical volume measure, including dimension zero. Let V:E -> R be twice continuously differentiable. Let alpha and beta be nonnegative real constants with alpha > 0 and alpha <= beta. Assume, for every x,v in E, that
alpha ||v||^2 <= (D(DV)(x)[v])[v] <= beta ||v||^2.
Here D is the totalized real Frechet derivative and grad V is the real Hilbert-space gradient. Let eta > 0 satisfy beta eta <= 1. Let rho be a real number satisfying 0 < rho < 1.

The following definitions are part of the statement. Every real division, including division by zero, is totalized; real division by zero equals zero. Subtraction of nonnegative real times is truncated at zero.

Write Omega = R^N with its coordinate-product measurable structure. Let P be the countable product of unit-rate exponential probability laws on R. For every sample s in Omega and integer k >= 0, put epsilon_s(k) = max(s(k),0), regarded as a nonnegative real.

For y,r in E define c(y,r)=y-eta grad V(r). For z=(u,v) in E x E and real t define the deterministic flow
Phi(y,r,t,(u,v)) =
(c(y,r) + cos(t)(u-c(y,r)) + sqrt(eta) sin(t) v,
 -sin(t)/sqrt(eta) (u-c(y,r)) + cos(t) v).
Put d_r(u)=grad V(u)-grad V(r). Define the reflection and nonnegative rate by
S(r,(u,v))=(u, v-[2 <v,d_r(u)>/||d_r(u)||^2] d_r(u)),
lambda(r,(u,v))=sqrt(eta) max(0,<v,d_r(u)>).
Thus the displayed reflection remains defined when d_r(u)=0, using totalized division.

For each nonnegative real t set
Lambda(y,r,z,t)=integral from 0 to t of lambda(r,Phi(y,r,s,z)) ds.
For a nonnegative threshold e let tau(y,r,z,e) be the infimum, in the nonnegative reals with an added largest element infinity, of all nonnegative t with Lambda(y,r,z,t)-e >= 0. The infimum of the empty set is infinity. This is the hittingAfter construction starting at time zero; no additional first-hit or conditional-distribution property is presumed.

For any y,r,z0 and any sequence e:N -> [0,infinity), define live/stopped records recursively. A live record is a pair (a,z), where a is a finite nonnegative accumulated time and z is in E x E; a stopped record is a separate absorbing symbol. Record_0 is the live record (0,z0). To obtain Record_(k+1), leave a stopped record stopped. From a live record (a,z), if tau(y,r,z,e(k)) is infinity, output the stopped record. Otherwise, writing h for that finite hitting time, output the live record (a+h, S(r,Phi(y,r,h,z))). Equivalently, the finite time is obtained by untopD 0, which returns zero at infinity, but the infinity case is checked first. Define T_n(y,r,z0,e) to be the accumulated time in Record_n if that record is live, and infinity if it is stopped.

For any real measurable exponent h, the notation Tilt(h) below means the probability-normalized exponential tilt of canonical volume, defined literally by density
x |-> ofReal(exp(h(x)) / integral exp(h) dvolume).
The normalizing integral is the totalized real integral. The definition alone does not assert that its value is positive or finite. Define
q_y = Tilt(x |-> -V(x)-||x-y||^2/(2 eta)),
mu = Tilt(x |-> -V(x)).
Let gamma be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian measure on E. Define
M_y = (q_y x gamma) x P
on (E x E) x Omega, with a point written w=((r,v),s) in precisely that order. Put t_pi=pi, considered as a nonnegative time. Define J on E x E as the pushforward of mu x gamma by
(x,v) |-> (x, x+sqrt(eta) v).

Then mu and J are probability measures. Moreover there exist Z, R, H, and K, with the existential dependencies specified below, satisfying all of the following.

First there exists a map
Z:E x E x (E x E) x [0,infinity) x Omega -> E x E,
written Z(y,r,z0,t,s), which is jointly measurable for the product measurable structures. Explicitly, the map (((y,r),z0),(t,s)) |-> Z(y,r,z0,t,s) is measurable.

For every y,r in E, every z0 in E x E, every sample s in Omega, every nonnegative time t, every integer n >= 0, and every live-record value a=(a_time,a_state), if
T_n(y,r,z0,epsilon_s) <= t < T_(n+1)(y,r,z0,epsilon_s)
and Record_n(y,r,z0,epsilon_s) is the live record a, then
Z(y,r,z0,t,s)=Phi(y,r,t-a_time,a_state).
The comparisons with event times take place in the extended nonnegative reals; t-a_time is nonnegative-real truncated subtraction, then included in R. Thus these equalities apply on the half-open intervals including an event's time at their left endpoint.

For every y,r,z0,s,t in those same domains, if there is no integer n >= 0 with
T_n(y,r,z0,epsilon_s) <= t < T_(n+1)(y,r,z0,epsilon_s),
then Z(y,r,z0,t,s)=z0. Both this fallback law and the preceding segment law hold for every sample, not only almost every sample.

For every fixed y,r in E and fixed z0 in E x E, for P-almost every sample s, the following conjunction holds: simultaneously for every nonnegative t there exist an integer n >= 0 and a live-record value a=(a_time,a_state) such that
T_n(y,r,z0,epsilon_s) <= t < T_(n+1)(y,r,z0,epsilon_s),
Record_n(y,r,z0,epsilon_s) is the live record a,
a_time <= t,
t-a_time < tau(y,r,a_state,epsilon_s(n)),
and Z(y,r,z0,t,s)=Phi(y,r,t-a_time,a_state);
and also Z(y,r,z0,0,s)=z0. The residual-time comparison again uses the extended nonnegative reals. The exceptional P-null set may depend on y,r,z0, but for fixed y,r,z0 this assertion holds for all t on one full-measure set.

For such a Z there exists a measurable Markov kernel R from E to E, every fiber of which is a probability measure, with R(y)=q_y for every y in E.

For such Z and R there exists a measurable Markov kernel H from E x E to E, every fiber of which is a probability measure, satisfying the following four assertions.

For every y in E, the kernel x |-> H(y,x) is reversible with respect to q_y: for every pair of measurable sets A,B in E, the nonnegative extended-real integral of H(y,x)(B) over x in A with measure q_y equals the corresponding integral of H(y,x)(A) over x in B with measure q_y. This is measurable-rectangle detailed balance.

For every y,x in E,
H(y,x) is the pushforward of M_y by
((r,v),s) |-> first_coordinate(Z(y,r,(x,v),t_pi,s)).
Thus its prescribed sampling order is a reference r with law q_y, a Gaussian velocity v, and exponential sample s under their displayed product law; the initial position in Z is the fixed x.

For every y,x in E, the pushforward of M_y by
((r,v),s) |-> Z(y,r,(x,v),0,s)
is exactly delta_x x gamma on E x E.

For every fixed y,x in E, for M_y-almost every w=((r,v),s), both of the following hold: Z(y,r,(x,v),0,s)=(x,v); and there exist an integer n >= 0 and a live-record value a=(a_time,a_state) such that
T_n(y,r,(x,v),epsilon_s) <= t_pi < T_(n+1)(y,r,(x,v),epsilon_s),
Record_n(y,r,(x,v),epsilon_s) is the live record a,
a_time <= t_pi,
t_pi-a_time < tau(y,r,a_state,epsilon_s(n)),
and Z(y,r,(x,v),t_pi,s)=Phi(y,r,t_pi-a_time,a_state).
This M_y-null exceptional set may depend on y,x. It is not asserted to be uniform in those parameters.

In addition, let nu be the pushforward of J under coordinate swap, so nu has coordinate order (auxiliary coordinate, position). Then R is a conditional kernel for nu in the measure-level sense
nu.fst compProd R = nu.
That is, composing the first marginal of nu with R reconstructs the whole measure nu. This identity alone is not a claim that conditional distributions are pointwise characterized on null fibers; the separate assertion R(y)=q_y holds for every y.

Finally, for such Z,R,H there exists a measurable Markov kernel K from E x E to E x E which leaves J invariant in one step:
J.bind K = J.
For every z=(x,b) in E x E, put u=2x-b. Its fiber is exactly
K(x,b) = [ofReal(rho) q_u + ofReal(1-rho) H(u,x)] x delta_u,
where the weights are nonnegative extended-real weights on measures. Since 0<rho<1, equivalently first compute the reflected auxiliary value u=2x-b, then draw a new first coordinate x_new with probability rho from q_u and with probability 1-rho from H(u,x), and return the ordered pair (x_new,u). The retained second coordinate is the reflected old pair value u, not the old b or x, and the H branch is indexed by (u,x).

The witness order is: probability of mu and J; there exists Z with all its measurability, pathwise, fallback and fixed-parameter P-almost-everywhere laws; then there exists R with its Markov and q-fiber laws; then there exists H with all its stated laws and the conditional-kernel identity for R; then there exists K with its Markov, J-invariance and all-fiber transition laws. All witnesses are under the original universal space, potential and parameter assumptions. No convergence, phase-process Markov property, temporal conditional-distribution identity, or invariance/reversibility of a process other than the explicitly named kernels is an additional conclusion.
objects: E, V, alpha, beta, eta, rho; Omega=R^N; P=product Exp(1); epsilon_s(k)=max(s(k),0); c; Phi; S; lambda; Lambda; tau; the absorbing live/stopped record recursion and event times T_n; normalized tilted measures q_y and mu; standard Gaussian gamma; M_y=(q_y x gamma) x P; t_pi=pi; J=(x,v |-> (x,x+sqrt(eta)v))_*(mu x gamma); existential jointly measurable Z; Markov kernels R:E -> E, H:E x E -> E and K:E x E -> E x E; nu=swap_*J.
domains: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed additive group with Borel measurable structure and canonical volume, allowing dimension zero. V:E -> R; alpha,beta in nonnegative reals; eta,rho in R. Samples are arbitrary real sequences, while exponential thresholds, record times and process times are nonnegative reals. Hitting times and event times take values in nonnegative reals with infinity adjoined. Phi accepts real times. Phase states are ordered position/velocity pairs. M_y coordinates are ((reference,velocity),sample), and J,K coordinates are ordered position/auxiliary pairs.
quantifiers: All space, potential, parameter and hypothesis binders are universal. The conclusion is IsProbability(mu) AND IsProbability(J) AND exists Z. For that single Z: joint measurability; for all y,r,z0,s,t,n,a the segment implication; for all y,r,z0,s,t the fallback implication; and for all y,r,z0, P-almost every s, ((for every nonnegative t, there exist n,a satisfying the six listed interval/record/residual/flow conditions) AND Z(y,r,z0,0,s)=z0). Then there exists R with Markov fibers and R(y)=q_y for every y. Then there exists H with Markov fibers, reversibility for every y and all measurable A,B, the time-pi pushforward equality for every y,x, the time-zero pushforward equality for every y,x, and for every fixed y,x, M_y-almost every w, (the time-zero state equality AND there exist n,a satisfying the six listed time-pi interval/record/residual/flow conditions). After that whole almost-everywhere clause, not inside it, is the unconditional IsCondKernel(swap_*J,R) conjunction. Finally there exists K with Markov fibers, J.bind K=J, and the displayed fiber transition for every z. The existential nesting is Z, R, H, K, with every earlier witness in scope for later witnesses and all original universal binders in scope throughout.
assumptions: alpha,beta >= 0; alpha>0; alpha<=beta; V is C^2; for every x,v in E, alpha||v||^2 <= (D(DV)(x)[v])[v] <= beta||v||^2; eta>0; beta eta<=1; 0<rho<1. All other supplied structures and literal definitions are given. No dimension-positivity, separately assumed normalizer positivity/finiteness, initial-state distribution, uniform parameter-null set, or process temporal Markov assumption is added.
conclusion: The normalized target mu and auxiliary joint law J are probability measures. There exist the jointly measurable segment-realizing process map Z with its explicit totalized fallback and fixed-parameter almost-sure all-time interval coverage, Markov R equal everywhere to q_y, Markov H reversible fiberwise under q_y and equal to the prescribed time-pi position law with both its initial law and its M_y-almost-everywhere endpoint realization, a measure-level conditional-kernel identity for R under swap_*J, and Markov K invariant for J with K(x,b)=[rho q_(2x-b)+(1-rho)H(2x-b,x)] x delta_(2x-b). The statement does not claim convergence or a temporal conditional law for Z.
scopes: All-sample segment and fallback identities quantify y,r,z0,s,t independently; the segment identity further quantifies n and a, subject to its three antecedents. For every fixed y,r,z0 there is a P-full-measure set of samples on which simultaneously every t has an interval/record witness and Z(0)=z0; the full-measure set may depend on those three fixed parameters. For every fixed y,x there is an M_y-full-measure set of w on which simultaneously the initial state equality and the existential time-pi interval/record realization hold; the full-measure set may depend on y,x. Reversibility holds for every y and all measurable rectangles. The pushforward equalities and kernel fibers hold for every displayed y,x or z, not merely almost everywhere. IsCondKernel reconstructs the swapped joint measure via its first marginal; invariance concerns K and J only. Witness dependencies are nested Z, then R, then H, then K under all initial assumptions.
constant_dependencies: There is no unspecified constant. alpha,beta control the Hessian and constrain eta through beta eta<=1. eta controls the center, oscillator scaling, rate, q_y normalization, and J. The event thresholds have unit-rate exponential law; the velocity is standard centered identity-covariance Gaussian; the fixed flow horizon is exactly pi; the reflection coefficient and final auxiliary reflection both contain the exact factor 2; the q_y penalty is ||x-y||^2/(2 eta); the final mixture weights are exactly rho and 1-rho. rho is strictly between 0 and 1. No spectral, dimension-dependent, asymptotic or convergence-rate constant is asserted.
